**VITRONAUT – Smart Astronaut Health Monitoring System**

VITRONAUT is an interactive health monitoring platform designed to support astronaut safety during space missions. As astronauts face health risks caused by microgravity, radiation, psychological stress, and limited access to immediate medical assistance, continuous health monitoring becomes essential.

Our solution brings together vital signs, such as heart rate, oxygen saturation, respiratory rate, and body temperature, alongside environmental indicators, including cabin temperature, radiation levels, CO₂ concentration, and humidity, in one unified dashboard.

VITRONAUT features an interactive 3D astronaut model, real-time data visualization, automated alerts when abnormal readings are detected, and guidance to help crew members respond appropriately. The platform also allows astronauts to monitor the health status of their fellow crew members.

Our current prototype demonstrates these capabilities using simulated data, with the potential for future integration with wearable devices and spacecraft sensors.

**Our mission is to transform complex health data into clear, actionable insights, enabling faster decisions and supporting greater crew autonomy during long-duration space missions.**

## VITRONAUT – Project Details

VITRONAUT is an interactive astronaut health monitoring platform developed for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. It aims to improve astronaut safety by combining vital signs and spacecraft environmental data into one centralized dashboard.

The system monitors health indicators such as heart rate, oxygen saturation, respiratory rate, and body temperature, alongside environmental factors including radiation, CO₂ levels, cabin temperature, and humidity.

VITRONAUT features an interactive 3D astronaut model, real-time data visualization, crew-wide health monitoring, automated alerts, and guidance to support appropriate responses when abnormal readings are detected.

The platform follows four main steps: **data collection, analysis, alert generation, and response guidance**. Its current prototype uses simulated data and predefined reference thresholds to demonstrate these functions.

Unlike traditional monitoring interfaces that focus primarily on displaying measurements, VITRONAUT emphasizes combining information into clear, actionable insights.

Future development includes integration with real wearable devices and spacecraft sensors, personalized health monitoring, and improved alert accuracy.

**Our goal is to support faster health assessments, informed decisions, and greater crew autonomy during long-duration space missions.**
